thread:
maya: Heads-up — we've got a product ask to make reranker fallback ordering deterministic across regions. Currently some customers see different candidate orders after fallbacks.
jon: Ugh, seen that. It's because we mix score sources (primary model score + reranker delta) and then apply different tie-breakers per region.
priya: Can we normalize the score envelope from the reranker so fallback sorting is stable? e.g. always expose an explicit "score_source" and "score_norm" in the API.
sam: I like exposing metadata. Consumers need to know whether a value is a logit, probability, or custom ranking unit.
alex: +1. Also need to think quotas — rerank endpoint charges per candidate scored. With fallbacks we double/ triple charge if we re-score. We should define "effective_candidate_units" in telemetry.
maya: Proposal: rerank response must include: `scores: [{id, raw_score, normalized_score, score_source}]`, and a `meta.fallback_chain: ["model-a-v2","model-b-quant"]`. That makes sorting and billing reproducible.
cheng: small nit: normalized_score format? float [0..1] or int percents? ops prefers ints for dashboard histograms.
priya: prefer float for precision; dashboards can bucket floats. But to keep parity with other endpoints we could do a 0-100 integer.
jon: Can we add `score_scale` field instead, e.g. `score_scale: "0-1"` or `"logit"`? Then clients can interpret.
sam: Billing side needs a single integer candidate count per response. If fallback triggers extra models, we must report `candidate_units` and `model_units` separately.
maya: OK decision draft: include `scores[]` with `raw_score` (stringified float), `norm_score` (stringified float 0..1), `score_scale` string, `score_source` string. Add `telemetry.candidate_units` and `telemetry.model_units` as ints. + `meta.fallback_chain` list of model tags.
alex: Sounds reasonable. Few edgecases: 1) If fallback is applied mid-stream (after partial streaming) — we need a deterministic merge strategy. 2) If clients request compact format (array of floats) for latency, we should provide a compact mode but still send a `telemetry` header with mappings.
cheng: For compact mode we can return `scores_compact: [0.81,0.72,...]` and `ids_compact: ["c1","c2"]` and still include `compact_mapping: {"format":"norm_0_1"}` in meta. But careful: agents.md — I mean, our docs — should warn about losing score provenance.
priya: Rollout UX: in Console when enabling a canary reranker we should show both model_units and delta_cost_per_call and a projected monthly cost. Also expose a simple toggle: "preserve_stable_order_on_fallback" default on.
jon: Telemetry fields to add to tracing: `rerank.fallback_reason`, `rerank.models_tried`, `rerank.model_affinity` so ops can alert on excessive fallbacks.
maya: I'll PR the API spec. Quick example payload to include in spec:
```json
{
  "request_id":"req-345",
  "candidates":["c1","c2","c3"],
  "scores":[{
    "id":"c1",
    "raw_score":"1.23",
    "norm_score":"0.9123",
    "score_source":"reranker-v3",
    "score_scale":"logit_to_0_1"
  }],
  "telemetry":{
    "candidate_units":"3",
    "model_units":"6"
  },
  "meta":{
    "fallback_chain":"[\"reranker-v3\",\"reranker-v2-quant\"]"
  }
}
```
priya: Can you include a snippet for the dashboard query? ops wants a per-route cost formula.
maya: Will add. Also adding a compat note: older SDKs that expect `scores: [float]` will keep working if we add `scores_compact`, but we should mark `scores` object mode as the canonical form.
alex: Deploy-bot FYI: any new telemetry fields need a backend schema migration.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created migration ticket INF-4621 for new telemetry columns and dashboards.
jon: OK timeline — spec PR today, schema migration + api impl next week, Console UX in two sprints. Anyone object?
cheng: no objections. :thumbsup:
maya: Cool, I'll file PR and link it here. Ending thread.
